nodes.statement: Erdős Problem 3: reciprocal divergence should force arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

For dyadic block density δ_j(A)=|A∩[2^j,2^(j+1))|/2^j, reciprocal divergence is equivalent up to a factor-two blockwise sandwich to divergence of Σ_j δ_j. Hence every nonnegative summable threshold θ_j is exceeded by δ_j for infinitely many j.
For each fixed k≥3, the reciprocal-divergence arithmetic-progression conjecture is equivalent to convergence of Σ_{n≥1} r_k(2^n)/2^n.
nodes.smallest_missing_estimate: A theorem-grade bound β_k(j) with r_k(2^j)/2^j ≤ β_k(j) and Σ_j β_k(j) < ∞, or an alternative bridge not reducible to blockwise density.
nodes.source_confirmation: Green–Tao 2017, Introduction; Tao–Vu, Additive Combinatorics, Exercise 10.0.6

nodes.statement: If r_k(N) is the maximum size of a k-AP-free subset of {1,...,N} and Σ_j r_k(2^j)/2^j converges, then every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains a k-term arithmetic progression.
Independently replay the dyadic mass sandwich, summable-threshold forcing lemma, and k-AP-free extremal reduction without using the native derivation.

supporting_nonpromoted_evidence.E3-Q01: Green–Tao 2017 is fixed-ambient; localization recovers only monotonicity.
supporting_nonpromoted_evidence.E3-A02: Literal submultiplicativity fails; strong multiplicative/power recurrences are constrained by lower constructions.
supporting_nonpromoted_evidence.E3-S03: Scoped primary-source audit found no post-2017 sequence-level estimate stronger than monotonicity.

nodes.statement: Let a_n=r_4(2^n)/2^n. Prove that there exist fixed L>=1, c>0, n_0, and 0<theta<1 such that a_{n+L} <= a_n(1-c a_n^theta) for all n>=n_0.
nodes.consequence: The discrete differential inequality gives a_n=O(n^(-1/theta)); since 1/theta>1, Σ_n a_n converges.
nodes.claim_boundary: Sufficient route only; it is not claimed necessary and is not proved by E3-X01.

known_falsification_boundary: Reciprocal divergence alone does not imply positive upper asymptotic density. More sharply, for every nonsummable threshold sequence θ_j∈[0,1], there exists a reciprocally divergent set whose dyadic densities never exceed θ_j. Thus summability is qualitatively sharp for any bridge using only blockwise density exceedance.
